# Lacuna v0.4.0

Lacuna `v0.4.0` completes the data-correctness milestone. It makes historical knowability,
revision coverage, and universe membership explicit evidence rather than implicit backtest
assumptions.

## Highlights

- Availability-safe as-of joins that preserve decision order, resolve ties only through declared
  revisions, enforce staleness and exact-boundary policies, and verify zero future matches.
- Direct future-data checks with affected-row samples and optional absolute materiality.
- Structural revision diagnostics that expose latest-only and unknown history rather than claiming
  point-in-time safety.
- Three-state survivorship evidence (`confirmed_safe`, `confirmed_biased`, and `unknown`) with
  planted delisting coverage and no unknown-to-pass conversion.
- Half-open historical membership selection with overlap rejection and a separate availability
  firewall for future-known membership records.
- Consecutive universe additions, removals, retention, Jaccard similarity, and drift evidence.
- Declarative dataset contracts for required fields, keys, nulls, numeric/temporal dtypes,
  non-finite values, and temporal ordering.
- Generated latest-nonfuture and half-open interval invariants, exact temporal fixtures,
  Polars/pandas/Arrow equivalence, and a versioned public as-of benchmark.
- A frozen additive `0.4.x` public contract that preserves supported `0.1.x` through `0.3.x` calls.

## Compatibility and distribution

This release keeps `AnalysisResult.schema_version == "1"` and adds the supported `lacuna.bias`
surface without removing earlier APIs. It is distributed as checksummed GitHub Release artifacts
because the `lacuna` name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project. The release workflow builds and
smoke-tests CPython 3.11 stable-ABI wheels for Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS arm64, and Windows x86_64,
plus a source distribution and provenance attestations.

The full implementation record is in the
[changelog](https://github.com/eyenoticeall/Lacuna/blob/v0.4.0/CHANGELOG.md). Exact temporal rules,
finding semantics, examples, and limitations are in the point-in-time data-correctness methodology
page.
